note: FACTORY-002 expose structured progress: src/factory/events.zig reads a stream of documents with a schema and hands the caller fields rather than substrings somebody hoped would be there. Validation is load-bearing: sequence numbers must strictly increase, so a repeated or backwards line is refused rather than applied twice; kinds are enumerated, so an unrecognised one is a schema error instead of being ignored; and a failure must carry a reason, because an agent that learns only that something failed has learned nothing it can act on. A line that does not open a document is refused as terminal text with its own error, which is exactly what a plain-text transcript is - and refusing it is the difference between reading the interface and scraping it. Writing the test sharpened the rule: prose and an array are different problems, so a line that opens a document is judged as one whatever shape it turns out to have. Fault proof: accepting a non-document line as a progress event makes the terminal-text assertions fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
